The catalog defines one disjoint group with members: LTM, CHO, CPC, CPAC — forming all pairwise disjoint relations among these 4 features.

To verify consistency, I need to compare the set of disjointWith edges in the graph (among Feature nodes, by name) against the set of disjoint pairs implied by the catalog's disjoint_feature_groups.

However, the catalog's disjoint_feature_groups content is source data (an answer literal set) that I'd need to embed — the feature names and group membership. The question asks whether the graph relations match the catalog. The catalog data is provided as a named source, but constructing the "expected" set requires hardcoding catalog member strings and the pairing logic as answer literals, which I'm instructed to avoid (no answer literals / supplied-source-derived truth as graph proof).

A source listing is not proof a graph edge/count exists, and I cannot derive the comparison purely from the graph schema without embedding catalog-specific feature-name literals and the group structure. The graph has no table representing feature_catalog.disjoint_feature_groups; it only has rel_disjointWith. There is no second graph-side source to compare against within SQL, so the consistency check cannot be computed from the database alone without injecting external literal sets.
